newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gypsy group asks Swiss for compensation for gold.
newsitem.headline: Gypsy group asks Swiss for compensation for gold.

text.p: The head of a Gypsy group urged the Swiss to compensate Romanies for gold stolen in World War Two that may have found its way to Switzerland, saying that as many as one million Gypsies were murdered by the Nazis.

In a letter to Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti made public on Wednesday, the head of the Swiss-based Romani Union said Swiss banks may still hold gold Nazis stole from Gypsies and melted down to hide its origins.
"It is an old tradition to dress up with heavy gold chains, rings and earrings or gold coins," Jan Cibula wrote, citing the Gypsy practice of carrying all their possessions with them.
"The Roma were certainly not incinerated along with their gold valuables, but were robbed of them. Some of them may still be here in Switzerland in melted-down form," he added.
"I...call on Swiss authorities to take these factors into consideration and to help compensate (us) through financing Gypsy organisations and cultural aims," he wrote.
The international Romani Union was founded in 1978 to represent the interests of Gypsy groups.

World Jewish Congress vice president Greville Janner last month urged Switzerland to pay compensation to Nazi victims now rather than wait five years for a report on Swiss financial dealings with Nazi Germany during the Holocaust.
"One has to wonder, are only Jewish valuables to be addressed?" Cibula wrote. "The Holocaust of the Jews was sufficiently recognised but the Roma Holocaust was recognised or compensated too little".
He cited historians' studies that as many as a million Gypsies were exterminated by the Nazis.
